title: Mike Read's Computer Pop Quiz
build: TAP of the original Elite cassette (1,530,784 bytes): a 512-byte Novaload boot program in the KERNAL's format, then 26 Novaload files: the loader's second stage, the loading picture, the program in four files, and five question blocks of four files each, which the game loads during play

records.c: The byte $51: high byte of the operand of `sbc $5146,x` at $4EFE (music driver, title part), the downward slide's subtraction, which straddles the boundary of this part. Not an instruction of its own.

The rest of the downward slide (from $4EFA): stores the lowered frequency ($510E), subtracts the slide speed's high byte ($5149) from $5111, then compares each byte with the note's frequency ($5165/$51C5 by voice_note $50E2): only when both the low and the high byte have dropped below the note's does it set the note's frequency and clear slide_dir ($514C). The bytes are compared separately, not as one 16-bit number.

End of each voice of music_play: writes the voice's frequency (freq_lo/hi $510E/$5111) and pulse width ($5114/$5117) into the SID registers at its offset (music_sid_offset $50C4), then goes on with the next voice (X - 1, back to $4C13) or, after voice 0, to the filter sweep. Reached from $4CA6, $4D87 (jumps in the title part) and the slides.

After the three voices: with no filter setting (filter_setting $5141 negative) writes $F0 to $D417 (no voice filtered, resonance 15); otherwise every filter_sweep_time ($541C) frames turns the sweep round ($5143) and moves the cutoff ($5142) up or down by filter_sweep_step ($5419), writing it to $D416 and the routing filter_route ($5413) to $D417.
music_filter_sweep: writes the new cutoff to $D416 and the routing to $D417.
Restores $FB/$FC, which music_play borrowed as its data pointer and saved on the stack at $4C03-$4C08, and returns from music_play.

A track byte $60-$6B (from $4C60): $6B stops the music (music_stop); any other jumps through the command table mcmd_lo/hi ($514F/$515A, index byte - $60) with X the voice (music_voice $50C3) and Y past the command byte (kept in music_read_offset $50C2).
`jmp` whose operand ($4FBB/$4FBC) music_command writes from the command table.
Low byte of music_command_jump's operand, written at $4FAA from mcmd_lo.
High byte of music_command_jump's operand, written at $4FB0 from mcmd_hi.
Command $6B: music_on ($50C6) = 0, so music_play returns at once from now on, and the gate of all three SID voices is cleared ($D404, $D40B, $D412).

`jmp music_exit`, the end of music_stop. In the quiz part this address is the sound-effects entry instead (X = effect); the title code calls $4FCB nine times ($09FF, $0D7F, $2F68, $2FB8, $30E0, $3131, $3138, $3171, $3178), all in rounds, after a question block has replaced these bytes.
Command $60 L, a rest: length index L gives the note time (note_lengths $525F into note_length $50F1), rest_flag ($50FA) = 1, and on to $4C96 (title part), which moves the read pointer on.
Command $61: toggles the voice's tie flag ($5100); while it is set a note's release and the filter restart are skipped. Reads on at $4C58.
Command $62 v: stores v in music_510D ($510D), which nothing reads (byte search of the title and menu code finds only this store). Reads on.
Command $63 v: volume v into music_volume ($510C), ORed with the filter type ($5145) into the SID's mode/volume register $D418. Reads on.
Command $65 n p t: plays pattern p n times (repeat_count $5109 = n) transposed by t; goes on into mcmd_call after storing n.

Command $64 p t (and the second half of $65): transpose ($5106) = t, the return address (after the command) into voice_return ($50D0/$50D3), the pattern's address from pattern_lo/hi ($5B1D/$5B36) into the data pointer $FB/$FC and voice_pattern ($50DC/$50DF); reads on from the pattern's start.

Command $66, the end of a pattern: while repeat_count ($5109) counts down to a non-zero value the pattern starts again (voice_pattern); then the data pointer returns to voice_return and the transpose is cleared.
Command $67: the track starts again from voice_start ($50D6/$50D9) with no transpose; the title tune's three tracks end with it, so the tune loops.
Command $68 lo hi: the voice's read pointer ($50CA/$50CD) becomes lo/hi, and reading goes on there (read_event, $4C4C).
Command $69 hi lo: the slide speed, high byte into $5149, low byte into $5146; the next note slides to its pitch at that speed (start_note). Reads on.

The last byte ($4C) of mcmd_slide's `jmp $4C58` at $5093. irq_setup calls $5095 ($2B58) only when effects_loaded ($33FE) is set, so the call always lands in the quiz part's sound-effects code, never in these bytes.

Command $6A f: filter setting f (0-2) into filter_setting ($5141): the filter type filter_mode ($5410 + f) into $5145 and, with the volume, $D418; the cutoff ($5416 + f) into $5142; the sweep counters cleared. Reads on.
The first byte of a note event, kept by $4C63 so that its bit 7 can be rotated in above the instrument's high nibble ($4C87).
Not referenced by the driver (byte search of the title and menu code): 0.
Y, the offset read so far into the voice's data, kept across commands ($4C74, $4FB7, $509C ...) and added to the pointer at $4C96.
The voice being played, 2, 1 or 0 (X), written at $4C13 and read back by music_command ($4FB3).
The voice's SID register offset, 0, 7 or 14 (from music_voice_offsets $33FF), set at $4C19; read by every SID write of the driver.
The voice's instrument (0-13), copied at $4C1F and $4CAF; indexes the instrument tables $527F-$5351.
Non-zero while the tune plays: set by music_init_body ($525B), cleared by music_stop ($4FBF); music_play returns at once when it is 0 ($4C09).
Three bytes 1, 2, 4: each voice's bit, ANDed with the filter setting's routing filter_route ($4D6F) to decide whether a new note restarts the filter sweep.
Three bytes: low byte of each voice's read pointer in its track or pattern (with voice_ptr_hi $50CD); set by music_init_body and mcmd_jump/mcmd_restart, moved on at $4C96.
High bytes of the three read pointers.
Three bytes: where each voice goes on after a pattern ends (low bytes; high at $50D3), written by mcmd_call.
High bytes of the three pattern return addresses.
Three bytes: each voice's track start (low; high at $50D9), for mcmd_restart; set by music_init_body.
High bytes of the three track starts.
Three bytes: the start of the pattern each voice is playing (low; high at $50DF), for a repeat in mcmd_end_pattern.
High bytes of the three pattern starts.
Three bytes: the note (0 = C0) each voice is sounding: the target of its slide and the base of its arpeggio.
Three bytes: the note read one frame ahead ($4C6C), with the transpose added; becomes voice_note at start_note.
Three bytes: each voice's instrument.
Three bytes: the instrument of the note read ahead ($4C8E).
Three bytes: frames left of each voice's note; 1 reads the next event, 0 starts it. Set to 2 by music_init_body.
Three bytes: the length in frames of the note read ahead (from note_lengths $525F).
Three bytes: frames until each voice's note is released.
Three bytes: the gate time of the note read ahead (from gate_lengths $526F).
Three bytes: 1 when the event read ahead is a rest (mcmd_rest), cleared by a note ($4C93).
Three bytes: the rest flag of the sounding event, copied from rest_flag at $4D64.
Three bytes: each voice's tie flag, toggled by mcmd_tie.

Three bytes: each voice's gate bit (1 while the note sounds), ORed into the control value of the waveform switch. The release at $4C31 (title part) writes `sta $5103` without the voice index, so it always clears voice 0's byte.
Three bytes: semitones added to each voice's notes (set by mcmd_call, cleared at a pattern's end and a restart).
Three bytes: how many more times each voice plays its pattern (mcmd_call_times).
The volume set by mcmd_volume (15 in the snapshot), kept to be ORed with the filter type.
Written by mcmd_set_510D and read by nothing.
Three bytes: low byte of each voice's frequency, written to the SID by music_write_voice.
Three bytes: high byte of each voice's frequency.
Three bytes: low byte of each voice's pulse width (from the instrument, then swept).
Three bytes: high byte of each voice's pulse width.
Three bytes: 0 while each voice's pulse width sweeps up, 1 down; turned at every end of pulse_sweep_timer ($4D9D).
Three bytes: frames until the pulse sweep turns, reloaded from instr_pulse_time ($52E1).
Three bytes: the frequency step of each voice's vibrato, from instr_vib_depth and doubled after the first swing ($4DF5).
Three bytes: frames until the vibrato swings the other way (from instr_vib_speed).
Three bytes: frames before the vibrato starts (from instr_vib_delay).
Three bytes: 0 while the vibrato raises the frequency, 1 while it lowers it.
Three bytes: set after the first swing, when the depth is doubled.
Three bytes: frames left of the arpeggio's step (the low nibble of instr_arpeggio).
Three bytes: each voice's place in its arpeggio table (Y of arp_read, $4E42).
Three bytes: the note the arpeggio last set (written at $4E5B); nothing reads it (byte search).
Three bytes: frames counted up to instr_switch_delay ($5351) before each voice's waveform switching starts.
Three bytes: frames until the next waveform switch (from instr_switch_period $5343).
Three bytes: which of the two control values (instr_switch_a/b) each voice has now.
The filter setting in use, 0-2, or $FF (none, the start value) when no mcmd_filter has run.
The filter cutoff written to $D416 by the sweep.
0 while the cutoff rises, 1 while it falls.
Frames since the sweep last turned.
The filter's mode bits (filter_mode $5410 + setting), ORed with the volume into $D418.
Three bytes: low byte of each voice's slide speed (mcmd_slide); 0 means no slide.
Three bytes: high byte of each voice's slide speed.
Three bytes: each voice's slide direction, 0 none (or arrived), 1 up, otherwise down (set by start_note).

Low bytes of the routines of track commands $60-$6A (eleven): mcmd_rest $4FCE, mcmd_tie $4FE3, mcmd_set_510D $4FEE, mcmd_volume $4FF7, mcmd_call $500C, mcmd_call_times $5006, mcmd_end_pattern $503B, mcmd_restart $5065, mcmd_jump $5079, mcmd_slide $5087, mcmd_filter $5096.
High bytes of the eleven command routines.
96 bytes: low byte of the SID frequency of notes 0-95 (C0 to B7); high bytes at freq_table_hi $51C5.
96 bytes: high byte of the SID frequency of notes 0-95.

music_init's body (jumped to from $4C00 with A = the tune): writes A into its own `adc #` ($522B) to index the tune table at 3 x A, copies the tune's three track addresses (tune_track_lo/hi $541F/$5422) into voice_ptr and voice_start, sets each note_countdown to 2, zeroes the SID's 24 registers, sets the volume to 15 and music_on.
16 note lengths in frames, chosen by the low nibble of a note's second byte: 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144, 192, 8, 16, 32.
16 gate times in frames, one for each note length: 2, 2, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96, 144, 6, 10, 28.
Instruments 0-13 (14 bytes, one each, like every instrument table up to $535E): the SID control value (waveform with the gate bit) a note starts with: $41 pulse, $81 noise, $21 sawtooth.
Instruments 0-13: the control value written at a note's release (the gate bit cleared).
Instruments 0-13: the attack/decay value.
Instruments 0-13: the sustain/release value.
Instruments 0-13: the starting pulse width, low byte.
Instruments 0-13: the starting pulse width, high byte.
Instruments 0-13: the pulse-width sweep's step a frame (0: no sweep).
Instruments 0-13: frames before the pulse sweep turns.
Instruments 0-13: the vibrato's frequency step (0: no vibrato).
Instruments 0-13: frames per vibrato swing.
Instruments 0-13: frames before the vibrato starts.
Instruments 0-13: high nibble the arpeggio table (arp_table_lo/hi), low nibble the frames a step; 0 for no arpeggio.
Instruments 0-13: the first control value of the waveform switch (0: no switch).
Instruments 0-13: the second control value of the waveform switch.
Instruments 0-13: frames between waveform switches.
Instruments 0-13: frames before the switching starts.
Low bytes of the eleven arpeggio tables ($5375, $539E, $53AB, $53B8, $53C5, $53D2, $53DF, $53EC, $53F3, $53FA, $5405), chosen by the high nibble of instr_arpeggio.
High bytes of the eleven arpeggio tables.

Arpeggio table 0: semitone offsets from the note, one a step, $7F starts again: 41 bytes in which an octave up (12) alternates with an offset that falls slowly from -2 to -7 ($FE 00 0C FF 0C FE 0C FE 0C FD ... 0C F9).
Arpeggio table 1: 0 4 7 4 0 4 7 4 0 4 7 4 (a major chord), $7F.
Arpeggio table 2: 4 7 12 7, three times, $7F (major, upper inversion).
Arpeggio table 3: 7 12 16 12, three times, $7F.
Arpeggio table 4: 0 3 7 3, three times, $7F (a minor chord).
Arpeggio table 5: 3 7 12 7, three times, $7F (minor).
Arpeggio table 6: 7 12 15 12, three times, $7F (minor).
Arpeggio table 7: 0 4 7 12 7 4, $7F (major, up and down).
Arpeggio table 8: 0 3 7 12 7 3, $7F (minor, up and down).
Arpeggio table 9: 0 3 0 3 0 3 ... continuing past $53FF into the title part ($5400-$5404); table 10 is at $5405.

Face 0 of the twelve stars of the team-picking grid, place 0 (top row, column 8), named "Mark" by the game (name entry 3, subject 0 Pop): a man with a dark quiff and round dark glasses, head turned. A face is 360 bytes in the game's picture format: 288 bytes of multicolour bitmap (36 cells of 8 bytes, 6 cells a row, 6 rows), 36 colour RAM bytes, 36 screen-colour bytes; it is picture 3 of the first picture table ($1773 ...), which draw_frame_block draws in the grid ($E75C) and copy_team copies into the players' pictures. The colour RAM and screen colours of this face are at $B920 and $B944.

Inside face 0's bitmap (the second byte of its first cell). The title code reads $B801 ($255C) as part of a question block's header, which the quiz part loads over these bytes; in the menu part it is picture data.
Inside face 0's bitmap (third byte of its first cell). In the quiz part, $B802/$B803 hold the block's word-list offset (read at $24EE/$24E6); here they are picture data.
Inside face 0's bitmap (fourth byte of its first cell); the quiz part's word-list offset, low byte, when a block is loaded.
Face 0's bitmap, from the fifth byte of its first cell. When a question block is loaded these bytes are its subject starts ($B804-$B80E, copied by $2AE5); here they are picture data.

Face 0's bitmap from its second cell on (to $B91F), then its colour RAM ($B920-$B943) and screen colours ($B944-$B967). The quiz part's first question record starts here ($343B reads $B80F) once a block is loaded.

Called once ($E8C3) when both teams are picked. Copies the six chosen stars' faces into pictures 1-6 of the second picture table: captain 0 (team_stars+4, $0B09) to picture 1 $8678, captain 1 ($0B0A) to picture 2 $87E0, the members $0B05-$0B08 to pictures 3-6 ($8948, $8AB0, $8C18, $8D80). For each it takes the star number's addresses from the first picture table (picture_bitmap $1773/$1782, picture_colram $1791/$17A0, picture_screen $17AF/$17BE) into the operands of four `lda $FFFF,y` loops: 256 + 32 bitmap bytes, 36 colour RAM, 36 screen colours. Then ($CB08) it copies the six names, and ($CBBC) repoints the drawing and the text printer at the copies. Returns at $CC0C.

High byte of the name address of star $0B0A (star_name_hi $AEA7), copied into name_captain_1 $1D43.

copy_team, part 8: writes $1749, $1750, $1757, $175E, $1765, $176C into the operands of draw_frame_block's six table reads ($1006/$1007 ... $1024/$1025), so that its pictures 0-6 are the second picture table (the host and the six players) from now on; then ($CBF8) points text_ctl_f1's name table (operands $37B5/$37B6, $37BA/$37BB) at $1D28/$1D2F, the seven name slots, so that `$F1 n` prints player n. Ends copy_team ($CC0C).
print_text text 1 (menu start-up, $E362): "  Select game options", ended by $FF. The menu's texts are ASCII, upper and lower case, each ended by , for print_text's sprite text panel.
print_text text 2 ($E374): "     One Player Game".
print_text text 3 ($E37D): "    Two Player Game".
print_text text 6 ($E615, $E712, $E820): "Player one".
print_text text 7 ($E61E, $E686, $E6BC): "Choose Specialist".
print_text text 8 ($E627, $E68F, $E6C5): "subject".
print_text text 9 (six calls, $E71B-$E88C): "Select team".
print_text text 10 ($E832, $E86E, $E895): "members".
print_text text 11 ($E724, $E7D0, $E7F7): " Captain".

print_text text 12, "Richard Underhill": one of nine panel credits (texts 12-20, to $CD0A) that no code prints; a search for every `jsr print_text` ($194C) found none with A = 12-20. The credits the player sees are the speech bubble's credits_text ($3E82).
Unused text 13: "Visuals by".
Unused text 14: "Steve Beverley". The printed credits ($3E82) say "Graphics by Dave Percival" instead.
Unused text 15: "Music by".
Unused text 16: "Mark Cooksey".
Unused text 17: "Game Design by".
Unused text 18: "      Ian Upton". The printed credits ($3E82) name Ian Upton and Nick Acton.
Unused text 19: "Copyright".
Unused text 20: "Elite Systems Ltd".
print_text text 21 ($E67D, $E7BE, $E85C): "Computer", for the second team in a one-player game.
print_text text 22 ($E6B3, $E7E5, $E883): "Player two".
$FF while the teams pick their captains, 0 while they pick their members: set at $E6EF, cleared at $E816 and $E84E; read by team_pick_frame ($CD3D, $CDA9).

Display state 2, once a frame (from the state table $06CB/$06DA): the team-picking grid. Counts menu_frame_count ($055E): at 1, when the cursor has moved ($0763) it frames the star under it (stamp_star X = $0761, the green mask unless changed) and, while members are picked, colours that star's subject icon in the picking team's colours (team_icon_colram/screen $EAB7/$EAB9); at 5 the count restarts and the input is read (team_pick_input). Other frames go straight to sprites_row0.
Operand of `ldy #$09` at $CD54: the screen colour highlight_icon gives the star's subject icon, written at $CD4E from team_icon_screen ($EAB9) by team.

Every fifth frame of state 2. Team 1 in a one-player game is the computer (cpu_team_pick); otherwise read_input. Fire (bit 4 low, not held, step_done clear): a new random cpu_moves_limit (8-11) and cpu_moves = 0; a star already taken (star_taken $0AF9) is refused; otherwise it is marked taken and star_flags_menu ($170B) = team (its frame colour), and the star number (place + 3) goes to the team's captain ($0B09 + team, then step_done) or to team_stars at member_count with its subject from star_subject ($0766) into team_subjects+2 ($0B0D); step_done when member_count reaches 2 and 4. Then the stick moves the cursor ($0761, 0-11) in the 4 x 3 grid: left/right within the row (column $0764, 0-3), up/down by 4 (row $0765, 0-2), each move first restoring the old place (restore_star).
The stick byte (from read_input or the computer) is stored in stick ($05D8) and acted on: fire, then the four directions.
team_pick_input: a captain or a team's second member was picked: step_done = $FF (the fourth member sets step_done itself, at $CDDC).
team_pick_frame's exit: on to sprites_row0, the text panel's interrupt.

The computer picking for team 1: while cpu_wait ($0B15) runs it repeats its last direction (cpu_subject_stick $0B16); otherwise it counts a move (cpu_moves $0B17) and, at cpu_moves_limit, presses fire; else waits 0 or 1 rounds (random) and takes a random direction of the four (direction_bits $0B11). Fire on a taken star is refused, and a new limit is drawn, so the computer wanders on and tries again.

restore_star's case for a taken star: redraws its frame (stamp_star) in its team's colours by pointing stamp_star's mask (operand $1529/$152A) at $9506 (red, team 0) or $952A (blue, team 1) as star_flags_menu says, then sets it back to the green cursor mask $94E2.

Called before each cursor move ($CDF3, $CE0D, $CE27, $CE45): keeps the place being left in $0762 and sets the moved flag ($0763); a taken star gets its team's frame back (frame_taken_star), an untaken one is redrawn without a frame (draw_frame_block, picture place + 3, at star_column/star_row $16F3/$16FF). Then ($CEF5) the star's subject icon gets its normal colours back (highlight_icon A = 1, Y = $CF).
restore_star's end: the subject icon of the star left ($0762) gets its normal colours (highlight_icon A = 1, Y = $CF).
253 zero bytes to $CFFF, the end of program file "3" ($4200-$CFFF); no reference found.
704 zero bytes ($E000-$E2BF), the start of program file "4" ($E000-$FF4A) as loaded; no reference found. A question block's files A and C later load over them.

The game's start, jumped to from $0503 after the hand-over. With the screen blanked ($D011 = $40) and black: sets up the display flags (sprite_enable_value, second_irq_on = $FF, irq_exit_port $25), zeroes the menu's and the round's variables, fire_held = $FF; seeds the random generator ($46/$47) from SID voice 3's noise (frequency $FFFF, control $80, read twice from $D41B); then irq_setup, make_mirror_table, clear_bubble, clear_shapes_4200, clear_panel, text_print (with text_ptr as it stands: $0000 at the start, so its first character is the processor port's direction register, $2F), copy_title_colours (the title picture's colour RAM from $F800), make_times8; copies the grid cursor's shape ($8EE8) to $4300; prints the options panel (texts 1, 0, 2, 3); scores_reset; draws the two options' bars (put_pixel_bar, $FF solid and $AA striped, 17 cells at pixel X $5C, Y $6F and $7F); then menu_flow ($E5A9).

Writes parameters for draw_strip ($E3F8: destination bitmap $6028, then $7428; menu_0571 0 then 1) and sets $01 = $25 twice, but never calls it: whatever call there was is gone, and nothing jumps to draw_strip.

Unused: no call or jump reaches it (byte search of the title and menu code). It would copy a strip of 30 x 8 cells into the title screen: colour RAM and screen colours from a source whose address it reads from $E99A,X (bytes of options_frame's code, so a leftover), and 240 bitmap cells from a bitmap address in $0572/$0574,X to the bitmap address set at $E39C, with the RAM under the I/O area switched in ($01 = $24, waiting for the interrupt when $1B72 is set). The 240-byte colour blocks at $EABB-$EE7A fit it, and the RAM at $D000 it would read holds only the power-on pattern.
draw_strip: low byte of the colour RAM source (`lda $FFFF,x` at $E436), written at $E40A from $E99A,X.
draw_strip: high byte of the colour RAM source, written at $E410 from the same byte $E99A,X as the low byte.
draw_strip: low byte of the colour RAM destination ($D800 + row address + cell_column), moved on by 40 a row ($E44E).
draw_strip: high byte of the colour RAM destination (row_addr_hi + $D8).
draw_strip: low byte of the screen-colour source (`lda $FFFF,x` at $E473), from $E99A,X ($E416).
draw_strip: high byte of the screen-colour source, the same byte $E99A,X ($E41C).
draw_strip: low byte of the screen-colour destination ($5C00 + row address + cell_column), +40 a row ($E48B).
draw_strip: high byte of the screen-colour destination (row_addr_hi + $5C).
draw_strip, the bitmap part: 240 cells of 8 bytes, 30 to a row (cell_counter $17), from the source at $E4D4 to the destination at $E4D7.
Operand of `lda #$28` at $E4BB: low byte of draw_strip's destination in the bitmap, written by the start-up ($E39E, $E3B9).
Operand of `lda #$60` at $E4C0: high byte of draw_strip's destination, $60 then $74 (written at $E3A3, $E3BE).
Operand of `lda #$00` at $E4C5: low byte of draw_strip's bitmap source, from $0572,X ($E3FE).
Operand of `lda #$D0` at $E4CA: high byte of draw_strip's bitmap source, from $0574,X ($E404).
draw_strip: copies one cell (8 bytes, X = 7 down to 0).
draw_strip: low byte of the bitmap source (`lda $FFFF,x` at $E4D3), +8 a cell ($E514).
draw_strip: high byte of the bitmap source.
draw_strip: low byte of the bitmap destination (`sta $FFFF,x` at $E4D6), +8 a cell and +$58 more after 30 cells, the next text row ($E4FD).
draw_strip: high byte of the bitmap destination.
draw_strip: moves the source on by 8 for the next cell.
The end of draw_strip: with $1B72 set it waits for the interrupt to restore $01 = $25 and turns the second interrupt back on.
Unused (no reference): copies 30 bytes from one `$FFFF,y` to another with Y from times8_lo ($4B00), i.e. one byte of each of 30 cells; both operands are never set.

Display state 14, once a frame after a specialist subject is chosen: flashes the chosen icon ($0761) through the team's colour list (team_flash_colours $3CEE from team_flash_start, the `lda` operand at $E573/$E574), a colour every third frame (flash_frame_count $3CE9, flash_colour_index $3CEA), screen colours team_icon_screen ($EAB9); each $FF at the end of the list counts flash_delays ($3CEB, 4) down, and at 0 sets display state 1 back and step_done. The text panel is hidden meanwhile (sprite_enable_value = 0); ends at irq_to_bottom.
Low byte of the operand of `lda $3CEE,y` at $E572: team_flash_start (0 or 7) + $EE, written at $E553.
High byte of the operand of `lda $3CEE,y`: $3C plus the carry, written at $E55A.

The menu's main line, from menu_start, each screen waiting for step_done: (1) game options (display state 0, options_frame): two_players = the cursor; games_left = 0 so that the first game asks for a question block; (2) "Player one / Choose Specialist / subject": the six subject icons (colour_face_block, highlight_icon) under display state 1 (subject_frame), then "Computer" or "Player two" for team 1; (3) at $E6D3 the twelve faces (draw_frame_block, pictures 3-14) for "Select team / Captain", player one then the other team; (4) at $E805 "Select team / members", two each; (5) at $E8A3 copy_team, the team screen with the bubble's credits ($3E82) under display state 4; (6) at $E916 the team introduction ($FE00) on the show's screen, the players' pictures appearing as Mike Read names them; then new_game ($2CD8).

Screen 3 of menu_flow: waits for team 1's subject, then clears star_taken and the picking variables, picking_captains = $FF, a random cpu_moves_limit (8-11); prints "Player one / Select team / Captain", clears three 6 x 6 colour blocks, draws the twelve faces at their places (star_column/star_row, pictures 3-14), frames place 0 (stamp_star) and runs display state 2 (team_pick_frame) until player one has a captain; then the same for team 1 ("Computer" or "Player two").
pick_captains: waits for player one's captain (step_done from team_pick_input).

Screen 4 of menu_flow: waits for team 1's captain, then picking_captains = 0, member_count = 0; "Player one / Select team / members" until team 0 has two members, then "Computer" or "Player two" until member_count is 4.

Screen 5 of menu_flow: waits for the last member, then three pauses (pause_state12), copy_team, the last star's subject icon back to normal, flash_mark = $FF; clears the play area, starts the bubble on credits_text ($3E82) and draws both teams (draw_left_team, draw_right_team), bubble colour 5, display state 4, until the text ends.

Screen 6 of menu_flow, once the credits have been said: starts the bubble on intro_text ($FE00), draws the show's frame (draw_show_frame), a new number grid (grid_setup, shuffle_number_order), the host (picture 0 at column 17, row 10), display state 4; each `$F0 n` event of the text (text_event $23, its n in $24) draws picture n at menu_place_column/row ($16D7/$16DE), so each player appears as named. When the text ends (step_done) it jumps to new_game ($2CD8), which asks for a question block because games_left is 0.

Display state 0, once a frame: "Select game options". Down (stick bit 1) moves the cursor (answer_cursor $0CB8) from One Player Game to Two Player Game, up moves it back; the two bars are coloured from the pairs at $0CBA,X (X = cursor x 2: 2, 0 or 0, 6) through the operands at $E9D7 (the first bar's colour RAM: red when chosen) and $E9E5 (the second bar's screen colours: blue when chosen); fire (not held) sets step_done. Ends at sprites_row0. Its first bytes also serve as draw_strip's mistaken colour source ($E407).
Operand of `lda #$00` at $E9D6: the colour RAM value of the One Player bar, from $0CBA + 2 x cursor (written at $E9C8; $E99C writes 2 first).
Operand of `lda #$02` at $E9E4: the screen colour of the Two Player bar, from $0CBB + 2 x cursor (written at $E9CE).

Display state 1, every frame (the stick is read only every fifth frame, menu_frame_count $055E): choosing the team's specialist subject. Team 1 in a one-player game jumps to cpu_subject_frame ($0B1B), which comes back at $EA36 with its stick in A. Fire (not held): flash_delays = 4, display state 14 (subject_flash_frame), team_subjects ($0B0B + team) = the icon ($0761, 0-5). Right and left step the highlighted icon round 0-5, putting the old icon's colours back (highlight_icon A = 1, Y = $CF); the current icon gets the team's colours (team_icon_colram/screen). Nothing stops team 1 choosing the same subject as team 0.
The stick byte in A (from read_input, or from cpu_subject_frame) acted on: fire first, then right/left.
`lda #1, sta team, jmp sprites_row0` after the `jmp` at $EA53: no branch or jump reaches it (references search).
subject_frame: colours the current icon ($0761) in the team's colours, then sprites_row0.

Operand of `ldy #$CF` at $EAAF: the screen colours highlight_icon gives the current subject icon, written at $EAA9 from team_icon_screen ($EAB9) by team; A, the colour RAM value, comes from team_icon_colram.
Two bytes, 1 and 1: the colour RAM value (white) of the highlighted subject icon for team 0 and team 1, read by subject_frame ($EAAC) and team_pick_frame ($CD51).
Two bytes, $2A and $6E: the screen colours of the highlighted subject icon, red and light red for team 0, blue and light blue for team 1; read at $EAA6, $CD4B and by subject_flash_frame ($E588).
240 bytes of $0B (dark grey): colour RAM for a strip of 30 x 8 cells, the shape draw_strip copies; nothing reads it (references search).
240 bytes of $5D (green and light green): screen colours for the same 30 x 8 strip; unread.
240 bytes, mostly 1 (white) with $0F and $A1 here and there: colour RAM for a second 30 x 8 strip; unread.
240 bytes of screen colours for the second 30 x 8 strip, mostly $62 and $69 (blue with red or brown), some $E9, $A2 and $AF; unread.
Zero bytes from $EE7B to $F7FF (2,437 in all, with zero_f204 and zero_f600 after the four labels at $F200-$F203); no reference.
Zero. The title code reads $F200 ($26AF) as section C of a question block (the Spot the Star offset), which the quiz part loads over these bytes; unused in the menu part.
Zero; with $F200 the Spot the Star offset of a block's section C (read at $26A6) in the quiz part.
Zero; section C's word-list offset in the quiz part (read at $268F).
Zero; the second byte of section C's word-list offset in the quiz part (read at $2688).
Zeros, continued from zero_ee7b, up to $F5FF.
Zero. Labelled because the boot loader jumps to $F4A5 ($0342), the KERNAL ROM's LOAD routine, which runs with the ROM switched in, not this RAM.
The last of the zeros, $F600-$F7FF.

The title picture's colour RAM image, 1,000 bytes ($F800-$FBE7, low nibbles; the high nibbles are ignored by the VIC), copied whole to $D800-$DBFF by copy_title_colours ($3ACC) at the start; the bitmap and screen colours are at $6000 and $5C00 in the title part.
Inside title_colours (row 0, column 23). Labelled because the boot loader calls $F817 ($0346), the KERNAL ROM's tape routine, with the ROM in.
title_colours from row 6, column 16 ($F900, the second page copy_title_colours reads at $3AD4).
title_colours from row 12, column 32 (the third page, read at $3ADA).
title_colours from row 19, column 8 (the fourth page, read at $3AE0), to the image's end at $FBE7.

24 bytes after the colour image ($FBE8-$FBFF): `71 0F 8D 1D 43 AD B1 0F 8D 45 43 ...`, which decode as stray code (stores to $431D, $4345, $436D): leftovers in the file, copied to the unused colour RAM $DBE8-$DBFF and otherwise unread.
304 zero bytes, $FC00-$FD2F; no reference.

32 bytes, the KERNAL's table of its 16 RAM vectors as it stands at $FD30 in ROM: IRQ $EA31, BRK $FE66, NMI $FE47, OPEN $F34A, CLOSE $F291, CHKIN $F20E, CHKOUT $F250, CLRCHN $F333, CHRIN $F157, CHROUT $F1CA, STOP $F6ED, GETIN $F13E, CLALL $F32F, user $FE66, LOAD $F4A5, SAVE $F5ED. Part of program file "4"; no code reads it (references search), so a leftover of how the file was made.
176 zero bytes, $FD50-$FDFF; no reference.

The team introduction, printed in the speech bubble by introduce_teams ($E92C): "Hello and welcome to the Commodore 64 version of (Mike Read's Pop Quiz).I'm Mike and here are the two team captains [F1 1][F0 1] and [F1 2][F0 2].The other members of [F1 1]'s team are [F1 3][F0 3] and [F1 4][F0 4].The other members of [F1 2]'s team are [F1 5][F0 5] and [F1 6][F0 6].So there are the teams and on with the game. Please select question block to load." then spaces and $7F (end, sets step_done) at $FF4A. `$F1 n` prints player n's name, `$F0 n` raises event n, on which introduce_teams draws player n's picture; ( and ) print as quotation marks.
Not loaded: program file "4" ends at $FF4A, so $FF4B-$FFFF hold the power-on pattern (00 00 FF FF ...), apart from the vectors the game writes at $FFFA and $FFFE.
Power-on pattern in this RAM. The game calls $FF84 (IOINIT, at $04FC) with the KERNAL ROM in, before it banks the ROMs out.
Power-on pattern. The block loader calls $FF90 (SETMSG, $2A64) with the KERNAL ROM in.
Power-on pattern. Labelled because the boot loader holds `sta $FFB2,y` at $0384 (its operand as the hand-over snapshot has it).
Power-on pattern. The block loader calls $FFBA (SETLFS, $2A70) with the ROM in.
Power-on pattern. The block loader calls $FFBD (SETNAM) four times ($2A79, $2A87, $2ABF, $2ACD) with the ROM in.
Power-on pattern. The block loader calls $FFD5 (LOAD) four times ($2A7E, $2A8C, $2AC4, $2AD2) with the ROM in.
The NMI vector the CPU reads while the KERNAL is banked out: irq_setup writes $0BE6 here ($2B32, $2B37).
The reset vector's place in RAM, not written by the game (power-on pattern); the boot program's `jmp ($FFFC)` at $02E2 runs with the KERNAL ROM in and so reads the ROM's vector.
The interrupt vector while the KERNAL is banked out: each raster handler writes the next handler's address here (seven writers, e.g. $046B, $04E5, $0681, $2B3C).
